purpose: Test autonomous second-order closure of geometry-fixed axial vector and its graph-cycle projection
input_scope: 36 already exposed primitive-periodic vertical stiffness matrices and4 fixed intralayer graphs; no new force model or physical bath
maps: C maps constrained material displacement into signed axial bond-vector increments; C_cycle applies graph P_cycle to each Cartesian component. Geometry frozen at each relaxed equilibrium. Same linear map applies to rates.
dynamics: qddot=-H q with H=Q^T Ksym Q, common scalar carbon mass absorbed into time. State observation is(Cq,Cqdot); full first-order velocity-only closure is not asserted.
exact_criterion: Exists L on range(C) with C H=L C iff ker(C) is H-invariant; equivalently C H N=0. For symmetric H, rowspace projector Pc satisfies Pc H(I-Pc)=0.
closure_statistic: ||Pc H N||F/||H||F where N is orthonormal hidden-space basis
uncertainty_diagnostic: Compare coarse/fine stiffness closure; resolved nonclosure requires leakage>1e-8 and>10 times(||Hfine-Hcoarse||F+||Hfine-Hfine^T||F)/||Hfine||F
witness: Relative-layer uniform breathing b, normalized in translation quotient, lies in ker(C) and ker(C_cycle); report visible acceleration C H b normalized by ||C||2||H||2. Also preserve SVD hidden-space witness of maximal coupling.
verification: Check map agreement against earlier response arrays, kernel residual<=1e-10, algebraic factorization residual via least squares, coarse/fine classification, independent projector/gauge calculation and all source hashes
rank_warning: Full column-rank observable closes by invertible encoding and is not evidence of a smaller independent channel
